description:
Content Editor (Copy Editing & Visual Review)
JOB DESCRIPTION
Job Title :  Content Editor (Copy Editing & Visual Review)
Company Name : NewAgeSys IT, (a division of NewAgeSys)
Location : Carnival Infopark, Phase 2 , Kakkanad, Ernakulam
Job Type : Onsite
Shift Timing : 11 AM - 8 PM
About the company
NewAgeSysIT , a division of NewAgeSys, Inc. established in 1994, based at New Jersey, specializes in mobile app development and consulting, helping clients maximize the reach and effectiveness of their business by leveraging the latest technology. Being a full service mobile and web development firm, NewAgeSMB focuses on servicing clients across North America, UK, Europe, Middle East, Singapore and Australia. We accomplish this by creating a long-term relationship with our clients, from brainstorming the initial idea, strategizing the project plan, building and deploying cost effective solutions with a solid foundation of support and maintenance.
Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced Content Editor to review and refine our business, technical, and marketing content. The primary objective is to improve clarity, readability, tone, and messaging while ensuring the content effectively communicates with its intended audience. The role also includes evaluating supporting visuals for relevance and communication effectiveness.
Key Responsibilities
Content Editing & Proofreading
Proofread content for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and consistency.
Refine language, sentence structure, and readability while preserving the original meaning.
Improve content flow, messaging, and tone to better engage the target audience.
Identify unclear, repetitive, or ineffective content and suggest improvements.
Ensure consistency with brand voice and professional communication standards.
Content Types Covered
Website pages, landing pages, and blog articles
Newsletters and client announcement emails
Case studies, white papers, and industry reports
Marketing collateral and other business communications
Visual Content Review
Assess the relevance and effectiveness of images, graphics, illustrations, and videos accompanying the content.
Evaluate how well visuals complement the message and connect with the intended audience.
Recommend improvements to visual presentation, including color schemes, background, tone, or image selection where appropriate.
Suggest alternative visual concepts when existing visuals do not effectively support the content.
Graphic design, image editing, and video production are not required.
Required Skills & Experience
Proven experience in professional copy editing, proofreading, or content editing.
Ability to refine content for clarity, engagement, and audience relevance.
Experience with B2B, technology, or professional services content is preferred.
Good editorial judgment and a basic understanding of visual communication.
Role Expectations:
The candidate should deliver polished, publication-ready content with clear editorial suggestions and actionable feedback on supporting visuals, within mutually agreed timelines.
Our Expectation: We are looking for someone who goes beyond grammar correction and can critically evaluate how effectively both written and visual content communicate the intended message to the audience.

Qualified lead targets and pipeline contribution from marketing
Team direction and weekly priorities
Ideal Customer Profile definition and content strategy approval

Budget allocation across channels
Marketing analytics and attribution
Hiring and building the marketing team

Writing content, designing assets, or running paid campaigns directly. This is a leadership and ownership role, where you set the direction, build the team, and are accountable for the outcomes.

8-12 years in marketing, with a minimum of 3-4 years in a senior or strategic marketing role.

B2B Content Specialist
2Base Technologies is at a deliberate stage of building its marketing function, and this role owns the written voice of that function end to end.
We are a technology services company with over 16 years of delivery experience, working with mid-market and enterprise clients across the United States and the United Kingdom. Our work spans AI implementation, custom software development, legacy system modernisation, and operational transformation.
This is a writing role with a specific, demanding purpose. It is not a content management role or a social media role. If that distinction is unclear from the outset, this is probably not the right fit.
What This Role Exists to Do
This role does not invent the voice. It operationalises, applies, and enforces it across all written output: long-form content that earns search traffic, content written in the voice of senior leadership for professional publishing, and the quality standard for everything written that leaves this company.
The audience spans technical leaders and business decision-makers at mid-market companies. CTOs and IT Directors who evaluate architecture decisions, and Founders, COOs, and Operations leaders who are accountable for technology outcomes without always having a technical background. Writing that works across that range, without oversimplifying for one end or losing the other, is the actual craft challenge of this role. Technically credible, commercially relevant, and written with a clear point of view. That is the standard this role is hired to meet and maintain.
What You Will Own
All long-form written content: pillar pages, blogs, playbooks, decision frameworks, and use-case libraries targeting senior decision-makers in the US and UK
Written content produced in the voice of senior leadership for professional platforms, which requires the ability to write convincingly as someone other than yourself
The 2Base content voice, including auditing all published content to ensure it meets the company's brand standards
Content briefs written clearly enough that a junior team member can produce a first draft without needing to ask clarifying questions
The content quality gate: nothing is published without passing through this role first
AI tool usage as a productivity layer, not as a substitute for thinking
What You Will Not Own
SEO keyword selection: the SEO Specialist sets this and you write within it
Social media scheduling and publishing: a separate team member owns this
Visual design of content assets: the Visual Designer owns this
Distribution strategy: the Marketing & Growth Lead decides which channels content goes to
ICP definition: you write for the ICP and you do not define it
What We Are Looking For
Experience
Minimum 4 to 6 years writing B2B content.
Has written content that ranked on Google, not just content that was published
Has written in voices other than their own, for executives, founders, or senior professionals
Understands SEO at a working level: knows what search intent means and can write to it without being an SEO specialist
Has worked with AI writing tools and knows both their value and their limits
Can show content that contributed to a measurable outcome: traffic, leads, or engagement with the right audience
Background in technology, SaaS, or professional services strongly preferred
Writing Ability
Writes with a clear point of view, not neutral summaries of other people's ideas
Can explain complex technical concepts in plain language without losing technical credibility
Writes concisely with no filler, no padding, and no unnecessary qualification
Can write in different voices and make each one sound authentic, not just adjusted
Mindset
Treats content as a commercial tool, not a creative exercise
Comfortable being edited and does not treat feedback as personal criticism
Genuinely curious about AI, technology, and business operations, not faking interest to get the job
Fast: this team moves at pace and cannot wait three days for a first draft
What We Are Not Looking For
Portfolios of "Top 10 Tips" articles or trend summaries with no original thinking
Writers who cannot explain how any of their content performed or what it contributed to
Anyone who has never written for a technical or senior business audience and considers that detail irrelevant
Writers who only produce self-directed content and have never worked consistently to a brief
Anyone who cannot write convincingly in a voice other than their own
Candidates who treat AI tools as the primary author and apply only light editing
An Honest Note on This Role
You will work with a documented marketing strategy and a defined brand voice from Day 1. You will take ownership of B2B content creation and help build the content workflow, writing briefs, and quality review process.
This role suits someone who enjoys writing for business decision-makers, translating technical concepts into clear content, and maintaining a consistent company voice. You should be comfortable taking initiative and building content practices as the team grows.
To apply, send your CV and two writing samples: one long-form B2B piece and one shorter piece written in a voice other than your own. If you do not have the second, tell us why in your cover note.
If this opportunity aligns with your career goals, kindly share your updated resume with us at
careers@2basetechnologies.com

Visual Designer
2Base Technologies is building its marketing function from scratch, and this role makes it look like a company worth taking seriously.
We are a technology services company with over 16 years of delivery experience, working with mid-market and enterprise clients across the United States and the United Kingdom. Our work spans AI implementation, custom software development, legacy system modernisation, and operational transformation.
What This Role Exists to Do
Before a CTO reads a word of our content, they see the design. Before they trust the argument, they have already made a judgment about whether this company looks credible. This role owns that first impression - and then owns every asset that follows.
The visual function at 2Base is being built from the ground up. There is no brand system to inherit, no template library to use, and no consistent visual identity to maintain. What exists is a clear strategic direction, a defined audience of senior technology and operations leaders, and a marketing team building the content engine around it. Your job is to give that engine a visual identity it deserves.
The first 30 days of this role have one priority: build the brand system. Everything else - LinkedIn carousels, ad creatives, landing pages, presentation templates — is built from that foundation. A designer who wants to jump straight into production before the system exists is not the right fit.
This is not a creative agency role. The audience is sceptical, senior, and technically literate. Design that looks clever but reads as unclear, or that feels consumer-facing rather than professional, will not work with this ICP. Restraint, precision, and consistency matter more than visual novelty.
What You Will Own
The 2Base visual brand system, including colour palette, typography, spacing, layout rules, and the documentation that makes it usable by the whole team
All marketing and content visual assets, including LinkedIn carousels, single-image posts, social graphics, infographics, and diagrams
Paid advertising creatives, including Google Display and LinkedIn Ads, designed to be tested and iterated
Landing page visual design, including layout, components, and conversion-focused structure, handed to the development team for build
Email visual templates, presentation templates, and sales deck templates
A template library that enables other team members to produce on-brand assets independently
Design consistency auditing, including periodic review of all published assets to ensure alignment with the brand system
Secondary responsibility: light video editing and motion for social reels, YouTube, and website use, supporting other team members
What You Will Not Own
What an asset communicates. The Content and Thought Leadership Specialist owns the message, argument, and information hierarchy. You may suggest improvements in structure, but content decisions remain with them
Copywriting. The Content Specialist writes the words; you structure them visually
Website development. You design the pages; the development team builds them
Content strategy. You execute what is briefed, not decide what gets created
Brand positioning. The Marketing Operating System defines how 2Base communicates; you interpret it visually
Experience
Minimum 3 to 5 years in a B2B design role, preferably in technology, SaaS, or professional services
Experience building a brand system or significantly evolving one, not just producing isolated assets
Experience designing for LinkedIn, including carousel formats, document posts, and single-image feed content
Experience creating paid ad creatives that have been executed, tested, and iterated
Experience designing landing pages with an understanding of conversion principles
Comfort with basic video editing for social and web content, including reels, short-form YouTube, and simple website assetsProficiency in Figma, which is non-negotiable, and Adobe Creative Suite including Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, and After Effects
Design thinking
Portfolio demonstrates restraint through clean, structured, and purposeful design
Ability to explain the reasoning behind key design decisions
Designs with a specific audience in mind, not for general appeal
Strong understanding and consistent application of typography as a functional tool
Ability to produce work that appears credible to a senior B2B audience at first glance
Mindset
Able to work effectively from structured briefs
Works at speed without compromising quality
Treats design as a communication tool rather than purely creative expression
Open to feedback and able to give it constructively
What We Are Not Looking For
Portfolios dominated by consumer brands, lifestyle work, event design, or campaigns with no B2B relevance
Designers who can describe visuals but cannot justify their decisions
Candidates without experience building a brand system
Designers who overcomplicate visuals with excessive fonts, colours, styles, or effects
Candidates who require complete creative freedom and struggle with structured briefs
Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

Sr.DevSecOps Engineer
2Base Technologies is a custom software development company with over 16 years of delivery experience. We work as an enterprise solutions partner for clients in the United Kingdom, the United States, India and other markets, building web and mobile applications and end-to-end digital solutions across industries.
We are adding a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to our DevSecOps team. You will strengthen our security posture, mature our pipelines and automation, and help the team build secure-by-design practice across everything we deliver. Depending on experience, this role can step into the lead position for the team or grow into it.
Key Responsibilities
Define, implement, and enforce security standards, policies, and best practices across cloud and on-prem environments.
Conduct security risk assessments, perform vulnerability scans, coordinate penetration testing activities, and execute mitigation plans.
Architect, maintain, and enhance secure CI/CD pipelines with automated compliance and governance checkpoints.
Promote and uphold a strong “Security First” culture across engineering, ensuring secure design and development practices.
Continuously monitor, detect, investigate, and respond to security threats, incidents, breaches, and anomalies.
Develop, own, and mature automation practices: infrastructure provisioning using Terraform and configuration management using Ansible, alongside other automation frameworks.
Design and maintain secure cloud architectures across AWS, Azure, or GCP to support scalable and compliant deployments.
Build, operate, and secure containerized environments using Docker, with enforced security baselines. Kubernetes where applicable to the project.
Implement and maintain secure monitoring, logging, and alerting systems for infrastructure and application layers, extending to SIEM as the practice develops.
Improve and optimize system reliability, scalability, performance, and fault tolerance across all critical workloads.
Mentor, guide, and upskill DevOps engineers in secure development, automation, and operational excellence.
Lead technical strategy, decision-making, tool selection, process improvements, and DevSecOps roadmap execution.
Work closely with PMO and engineering teams so that security, performance and delivery objectives stay aligned.
Operational Ownership
Backup and disaster recovery: Backup policies, regular tested restoration, and disaster recovery plans with agreed recovery time and data loss targets, with restoration tested rather than assumed.
Release management: Deployments across development, staging and production, including approvals, rollback procedures, and troubleshooting failed releases.
Access and secrets management: Access reviews, joiner and leaver access, service accounts, credentials, secrets rotation, and encryption keys.
Pipeline security: Code, dependency, container image, secrets and Infrastructure-as-Code scanning built into CI/CD, with clear ownership of who fixes what and by when.
Incident management: Leading production incident response, coordinating updates to the people who need them, running root cause reviews, and tracking corrective actions to closure.
Cloud cost management: Monitoring cloud spend, investigating unexpected cost, and improving resource sizing and utilisation without affecting reliability.
Documentation: Infrastructure diagrams, configuration records, deployment guides, operational runbooks and recovery procedures, maintained as the environment changes.
Reliability measurement: Defining and tracking service availability, deployment failure rate, recovery time, and how long vulnerabilities take to close.
Requirements
Required Skills and Experience
6–10 years of experience in DevOps, Cloud, or Infrastructure engineering, including at least 4 years hands-on in DevOps, with strong security exposure.
Strong hands-on expertise in AWS, with a focus on secure architecture.
Deep experience with at least one CI/CD platform, such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or Bitbucket Pipelines. Breadth across several is useful; depth in one is required.
Experience securing and running Docker containers in production.
Experience independently owning production infrastructure, releases and incident resolution, demonstrated through the work you have led.
Strong understanding of networking technologies: LAN/WAN, firewalls, VPN, load balancers.
Knowledge of security frameworks and standards (OWASP, NIST, CIS Benchmarks).
Working depth in at least one monitoring and logging stack, such as Prometheus and Grafana, the ELK stack, or CloudWatch.
Strong scripting skills (Python, Bash, Shell).
Excellent troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to influence engineering teams.
Tools and Technology
These are the areas you will be working in. Core areas are assessed during the interview process. Additional areas strengthen an application, and support is available to develop them in the role.
AWS: Hands-on work across compute, storage, networking, access management and cost, based on environments you have configured.
CI/CD: Building and maintaining pipelines in Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or Bitbucket Pipelines, including the security checks within them. Depth in one platform is sufficient.
Git: Version control in practice: branching strategy, merge and release flow, repository access control, and keeping credentials out of version history.
Cloud server administration: Provisioning, sizing, lifecycle and cost of the servers behind the applications, in the cloud and on-premise where it applies.
Ubuntu: Ubuntu Server administration at an operational standard: packages, services, storage, networking, DNS, TLS and permissions.
Monitoring tools: Prometheus and Grafana, the ELK stack, CloudWatch or an equivalent, implemented by you, with judgement about alert severity. Depth in one stack is sufficient.
Server security: Hardening, patching, firewall and SSH configuration, least-privilege access, and closing known vulnerabilities to an agreed timeline.
Terraform: Infrastructure provisioning as code.
Ansible: Configuration management and automation.
Azure: Working depth in the equivalent services, and judgement about what belongs where when a client runs more than one platform.
GCP: Relevant where a client workload sits there.
Kubernetes: Running and securing orchestrated containers in production, where a project uses them.
SIEM and SOAR: Security event collection and response tooling. Prior experience is welcome; where you do not have it, this capability is developed in the role with support.
Education
A degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field. Equivalent practical experience is considered on the same terms.

Legal Content Specialist (LLB)
This role sits between our legal reality and our readers. CookieYes publishes a large library of privacy content that businesses across the world rely on to understand what the law asks of them, and we need someone professionally qualified to stand behind it.
We are looking for a law graduate who writes because they want to, not because a brief demanded it. You will track privacy legislation across jurisdictions, translate it into content our customers can act on, and act as the internal check on the legal accuracy of everything we publish and ship. Part of the role is genuine legal work: reviewing our own agreements, supporting compliance queries from customers, and keeping our product claims defensible.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Monitor privacy and data protection developments globally, including GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA and other US state laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, PDPA and emerging regulations, and flag what matters for CookieYes and our customers.
Write authoritative long-form content: regulation explainers, jurisdiction guides, compliance checklists, legal update posts and whitepapers.
Act as the legal accuracy reviewer for marketing and product content, with an agreed turnaround SLA so reviews never stall the pipeline. Nothing that makes a compliance claim should ship without your reading.
Structure that content to be found and cited by AI search, AI Overviews and answer engines, working with the SEO and AI search team on generative engine optimisation, schema and citation-worthy formatting.
Translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, working with product and engineering on how consent, records and disclosures need to behave.
Support customer-facing compliance queries escalated by sales and support, and build the internal reference material that reduces how often they need escalating.
Review and maintain our own legal documents, including the privacy policy, terms of service, DPAs and vendor agreements, with external counsel where required.
Prepare briefing notes for leadership when a regulatory change affects roadmap or positioning.
Represent CookieYes’s point of view publicly through bylined articles, webinars and industry commentary.
REQUIREMENTS
LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognised institution. Enrolment with a bar council is welcome but not required.

About the role
We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus of the role is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements as needed, alongside supporting existing entities and reinsurance programmes where required. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build-focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady-state reporting.
Key responsibilities
Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) — defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, and ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet the requirements of the relevant regulator; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g. DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
Build the financial model for each new entity — three-statement model and entity-level profit and loss — establishing the management reporting suite from which ongoing reporting will run.
Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring the accounting treatment and control framework are correctly set up from inception; support existing programmes as required.
Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity-level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing the format, commentary structure and distribution; support the ongoing production of these for existing entities as required.
Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) — providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for completion of the annual capital setting process (ECM/SBF cycle), optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining the FAL headroom analysis relative to the approved capital requirement.
Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities — including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity — to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes — including letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits — ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed in line with programme terms and regulatory requirements.
Own the capital waterfall and inter-entity funding mechanics — managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, and ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
Produce the board-level capital reporting pack — including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes — on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, including covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day-to-day work.

5+ years experienced
DevOps and Infrastructure Engineer with strong networking fundamentals and hands-on BGP and IP configuration experience. You will manage and scale multi-cloud and on-premise infrastructure for our Kubernetes-native WAF/WAAP platform. The role also covers
Linux and Windows server administration and support for enterprise customer deployments.
Key Responsibilities
Design, configure, and troubleshoot network infrastructure across cloud, data center, and customer environments.
Configure and manage BGP sessions (eBGP/iBGP), route advertisements, prefix filtering, route maps, and failover with upstream providers and peers.
Plan and manage IP addressing, including IPv4/IPv6 subnetting, CIDR allocation, VLANs, NAT, and static and dynamic routing.
Administer Linux servers (Ubuntu, RHEL/CentOS, Rocky): provisioning, hardening, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
Administer Windows Server environments, including Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, IIS, and patching.
Deploy and operate infrastructure on AWS, GCP, Azure, and private cloud: VPCs, VPNs, transit gateways, load balancers, and security groups.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/Ansible), and containerized workloads on Kubernetes.
Manage firewalls, VPN/IPsec tunnels, DNS, and load balancers such as HAProxy, NGINX, and cloud LBs.
Set up monitoring, logging, and alerting with Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, or similar tools.
Participate in incident response and root cause analysis, and provide L2/L3 support for enterprise customers.
Document network topologies, runbooks, and standard operating procedures.
Required Skills & Qualifications
Networking (core requirement)
Strong understanding of the TCP/IP stack and the OSI model.
Hands-on experience with BGP configuration and troubleshooting, including AS paths, local preference, MED, communities, and route filtering.
Working knowledge of OSPF, static routing, ECMP, and route redistribution.
Expertise in IP addressing, subnetting, VLANs, NAT/PAT, ACLs, and IPv6.
Experience with DNS, DHCP, VPN (IPsec/WireGuard/OpenVPN), and load balancing.
Familiarity with network devices and platforms such as Cisco, Juniper, MikroTik, pfSense, or Linux-based routing (FRR/BIRD).
Proficiency with troubleshooting tools: tcpdump, Wireshark, traceroute, mtr, iperf, dig, ss/netstat.
Systems Administration
5+ years of Linux administration, including networking (iproute2, iptables/nftables), systemd, and storage.
Solid Windows Server administration (AD, DNS, DHCP, GPO, PowerShell).
Cloud & DevOps
Production experience with at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure); multi-cloud is a plus.
Cloud networking: VPC design, peering, Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect / ExpressRoute, hybrid connectivity.
Docker and Kubernetes (k8s/k3s), including CNI networking (Calico, Cilium, Flannel).
Terraform, Ansible, and CI/CD tools (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins).
Scripting in Bash, Python, or PowerShell.

Certifications such as CCNA/CCNP, RHCSA/RHCE, AWS/Azure/GCP Associate or Professional, or CKA.
Experience with anycast, CDN, or DDoS mitigation architectures.
Exposure to WAF, web security, or the cybersecurity domain.
Soft Skills
Strong troubleshooting and analytical mindset under production pressure.
Clear communication with customers and cross-functional teams.
Ability to mentor junior engineers and own projects end to end.

Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced
Technical Project Manager
to take ownership of project planning, technical team coordination, client communication, and end-to-end software delivery.
The successful candidate will act as the primary coordination point between clients, developers, testers, technical leads, and company management. The role requires a strong understanding of software development, the ability to manage multiple projects, and the confidence to drive accountability across teams.
The candidate must be proactive in identifying risks, resolving coordination issues, managing priorities, and ensuring that project commitments are met. They should be capable of independently managing day-to-day project execution while keeping management informed of progress, risks, and decisions requiring attention.
This is a hands-on project delivery role, not merely an administrative or reporting position.
Key Responsibilities
1. Project Planning and End-to-End Delivery
Take ownership of assigned software development projects from requirement clarification through development, testing, release, and ongoing maintenance.
Work with clients and technical teams to understand business requirements, scope, priorities, and expected outcomes.
Convert requirements into actionable tasks, milestones, delivery plans, and realistic timelines.
Estimate and coordinate effort, resources, dependencies, and delivery schedules with technical leads.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously while ensuring priorities and commitments remain clear.
Track planned versus actual progress and take corrective action when projects deviate from agreed timelines.
Ensure deliverables meet agreed requirements and acceptance criteria.
Manage scope changes, assess their impact on timelines and resources, and obtain appropriate approvals.
Maintain clear ownership of deliverables, outstanding actions, and upcoming milestones.
2. Technical Team Management and Coordination
Coordinate developers, QA engineers, technical leads, and other stakeholders to ensure smooth execution.
Understand technical discussions involving application architecture, databases, APIs, integrations, defects, hosting, and deployment.
Work with technical leads to assess estimates, identify dependencies, and evaluate delivery risks.
Review task progress and ensure developers provide timely and accurate updates.
Identify technical blockers and facilitate their resolution.
Challenge unrealistic estimates or commitments constructively and help establish achievable delivery plans.
Coordinate code reviews, testing, bug fixes, release preparation, and deployment activities.
Ensure development work follows agreed priorities, coding practices, and quality processes.
Monitor workload distribution and raise resource constraints or competing priorities with management.
Foster accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement within the technical team.
3. International Client Communication and Relationship Management
Serve as the primary day-to-day project contact for assigned international clients.
Communicate professionally with clients, including those based in the United States and Europe.
Lead project meetings, progress calls, requirement discussions, sprint reviews, and delivery reviews.
Provide clear and regular updates on completed work, current progress, upcoming deliverables, risks, and pending decisions.
Clarify requirements and ensure client expectations are translated into actionable technical tasks.
Manage client feedback, change requests, approvals, and dependencies.
Communicate potential delays early, explain their impact transparently, and propose corrective actions.
Manage expectations regarding scope, effort, priorities, and delivery commitments.
Handle project concerns and disagreements professionally, escalating significant commercial or strategic matters when necessary.
Maintain accurate records of client discussions, decisions, commitments, and action items.
4. Project Monitoring, Reporting, and Risk Management
Maintain accurate project plans, task trackers, milestone schedules, issue logs, and risk registers.
Monitor task completion, overdue items, unresolved defects, and pending client inputs.
Prepare regular project status reports for management and clients.
Track project health, delivery risks, resource dependencies, and schedule deviations.
Identify warning signs early and initiate corrective actions before issues affect delivery.
Ensure every significant issue has a clearly identified owner, target resolution date, and follow-up plan.
Escalate critical risks promptly with relevant facts, potential impact, and recommended next steps.
Maintain visibility into the status of all assigned projects so management is not surprised by preventable delays.
5. Software Quality and Release Management
Coordinate requirement analysis, development, QA, user acceptance testing, release, and post-release support.
Ensure appropriate testing and defect resolution before deliverables are released.
Track outstanding bugs, severity, resolution progress, and client acceptance.
Coordinate deployment schedules, release notes, implementation plans, and client notifications.
Work with technical teams to identify recurring defects and improve delivery quality.
Ensure project documentation and handover information are maintained.
Support incident coordination and prioritization when production issues affect clients.
6. Project Management Processes and Continuous Improvement
Establish consistent project planning, tracking, reporting, and follow-up practices.
Improve visibility into developer workloads, project progress, delivery commitments, and pending decisions.
Identify gaps in project ownership, communication, estimation, and execution.
Develop practical standard operating procedures and reusable project templates.
Use project management tools and AI-assisted productivity tools to improve reporting, documentation, meeting summaries, and workflow efficiency.
Review recurring delivery issues and implement corrective measures.
Recommend improvements to resource utilization, development workflows, quality processes, and client communication.
Ensure that project management practices remain practical and proportionate to the size and complexity of each project.
7. Management Coordination
Provide management with a reliable overview of project progress, risks, delivery commitments, and resource constraints.
Highlight decisions requiring management intervention, together with recommended options.
Support project prioritization and resource allocation discussions.
Identify recurring operational problems and recommend solutions.
Take independent decisions within agreed authority and escalate commercial, contractual, financial, or strategic decisions when required.
Reduce the need for management to follow up individually on routine project tasks and outstanding commitments.
Required Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in technical project management, software project delivery, or software development coordination.
Strong understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
Demonstrated experience coordinating software developers and managing project delivery commitments.
Experience communicating directly with clients and managing requirements, timelines, feedback, and expectations.
Strong technical understanding of web applications, databases, APIs, integrations, testing, and deployment processes.
Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects, competing priorities, and delivery risks.
Strong organizational, analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently, make sound operational decisions, and take ownership of outcomes.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Performance will be assessed against agreed targets, taking into account project complexity, approved scope changes, client dependencies, and technical constraints.
Delivery reliability:

description:

We are looking for a Full Stack Developer to build and deploy applications end to end, using AI coding tools as a core part of the daily workflow rather than an occasional aid. Review code from teams following the practice, including AI-generated code, applying consistent quality standards.
Incorporate delivery outcomes and feedback from adopting teams to refine templates, guidelines, and pipelines on an ongoing basis.

role: Senior Software Engineer – AI-Augmented Software Development-REMOTE:6+ Yrs
description:
Job Description
Experience Required: 6+ years (Remote)
Employment Type: Full-time
Package offered- 20- 30 LPA
About the Role
We're looking for a hands-on Senior engineer who primarily focuses on building high-quality software, with strong capabilities in evaluating code quality and owning end-to-end delivery across the SDLC . This person will work extensively with AI-assisted development tools and will be accountable for ensuring every deliverable — whether built internally, by vendors, or with AI assistance — meets high standards of correctness, quality, security, and compliance. You'll be the connective tissue between development, QA, the AI SDLC framework, vendors, and clients — driving execution while holding the line on engineering excellence.
Key Responsibilities
Development- Primary Responsibility
● Write, review, and refactor production-grade code across the stack as needed
● Leverage AI-assisted development tools to accelerate delivery without compromising quality or introducing technical debt
● Set and model engineering best practices: clean architecture, maintainability, performance, and scalability
Quality & Security
● Review deliverables with a QA mindset — functional correctness, edge case coverage, regression risk, and test adequacy
● Conduct security-focused code reviews (secure coding practices, common vulnerability classes, dependency risk, data handling)
● Define and enforce quality gates and Definition-of-Done criteria across the SDLC
● Ensure compliance with relevant coding, security, and regulatory standards
Delivery & Orchestration
● Own the complete SDLC lifecycle — planning, development, testing, deployment, and release
● Coordinate across development teams, QA, and the AI SDLC framework/tooling to keep delivery on track
● Act as the primary technical point of contact for vendors and clients, translating requirements and validating vendor deliverables against internal quality bars
● Identify bottlenecks or risks across teams/departments and drive them to resolution proactively
● Report on delivery health, quality metrics, and risk status to stakeholders
Required Skills
● Programming Languages: Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Python, C#, Go, or similar); ability to read and reason about code in adjacent languages is a plus
● Software Design & Architecture: Solid grasp of design patterns, clean code principles, and system/API design
● Testing & QA Practices: Familiarity with unit, integration, and end-to-end testing frameworks; ability to assess test coverage and quality, not just write tests
● Test Automation Frameworks: Hands-on experience with at least one automated testing framework such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, or similar — able to write, review, and evaluate automated test suites as part of the quality gate
● Security Fundamentals: Working knowledge of secure coding practices and common vulnerability classes (e.g., OWASP Top 10), plus basics of dependency and data-handling risk
● AI-Assisted Development Tools: Hands-on experience with tools like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar
● Version Control & CI/CD: Practical experience with Git-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar)
● Cloud & Infrastructure Basics: Working familiarity with at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containerization basics (Docker)
● Code Review & Static Analysis: Comfort using or setting up static analysis, linting, and code quality tools (e.g., SonarQube, ESLint, or similar)
● Communication & Stakeholder Coordination: Ability to clearly communicate technical decisions and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders (dev, QA, vendors, clients)
Required Qualifications
● 6+ years of professional software development experience, with strong hands-on coding ability in at least one modern stack
● Demonstrated experience reviewing others' code for quality, logic correctness, and security — not just writing code
● Solid understanding of secure coding practices and common vulnerability patterns (e.g., OWASP Top 10 or equivalent)
● Experience working with or evaluating AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar)
● Proven experience coordinating cross-functional stakeholders — development, QA, vendors, and clients
● Strong understanding of SDLC methodologies (Agile/Scrum, CI/CD pipelines, release management)
● Excellent communication skills to bridge technical and non-technical stakeholders

●    Programming Languages: Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Python, C#, Go, or similar); ability to read and reason about code in adjacent languages is a plus
●    Software Design & Architecture: Solid grasp of design patterns, clean code principles, and system/API design

●    6+ years of professional software development experience, with strong hands-on coding ability in at least one modern stack
●    Demonstrated experience reviewing others' code for quality, logic correctness, and security — not just writing code
●    Solid understanding of secure coding practices and common vulnerability patterns (e.g., OWASP Top 10 or equivalent)

●    Proven experience coordinating cross-functional stakeholders — development, QA, vendors, and clients
●    Strong understanding of SDLC methodologies (Agile/Scrum, CI/CD pipelines, release management)
●    Excellent communication skills to bridge technical and non-technical stakeholders

description:
Backend & Data Infrastructure Engineer
At Fingent, we believe that technology can make a meaningful difference to the lives around us. The lives of those who use it, the lives of those who build it and to society at large. We create and provide software which is beautiful, usable and compelling, to solve complex business challenges. We nurture smart people who bring out the best in themselves, their peers, and their clients.
About the Role
We are looking for a Hybrid Backend & Data Infrastructure Engineer to architect and scale the backend services and high-throughput data platforms that power our core products and analytical insights.
In this role, you will bridge the gap between software engineering, distributed systems, and data infrastructure. You will design high-performance microservices and APIs, orchestrate complex streaming and batch pipelines, automate cloud-native infrastructure, and solve hard distributed-systems challenges—such as multi-replica race conditions, state synchronization, and sub-second data processing.
Key Roles & Responsibilities
Backend & Microservices Engineering
Architect, build, and deploy low-latency, scalable APIs and microservices using modern Python (FastAPI, FastMCP, uv).
Integrate foundational AI/LLM models and external services (e.g., AWS Bedrock).
Define resilient service interfaces, API schemas, and data contracts between internal engineering teams.
Distributed Systems & Concurrency Management
Design robust state-management patterns to handle high-concurrency race conditions across worker pools, message queues, and database rows.
Implement distributed synchronization mechanisms (e.g., distributed locks/mutexes, idempotency keys, and optimistic/pessimistic locking strategies).
Ensure reliable execution, deduplication, and zero-data-loss guarantees across asynchronous task workers.
Data Infrastructure & Orchestration
Develop and maintain scalable job orchestration workflows for streaming and batch processing using Celery, Dagster, or Apache Airflow.
Design, optimize, and maintain relational datastores (PostgreSQL) and in-memory caches (Redis).
Build modern analytical pipelines and data storage layers leveraging Lakehouse architectures (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake) and Change Data Capture (CDC) patterns.
Enforce end-to-end data quality, governance, schema evolution, and lineage across platforms.
Cloud Infrastructure, Kubernetes & CI/CD
Own, automate, and maintain cloud environments on AWS using Infrastructure-as-Code (CDKTF / Terraform).
Containerize services with Docker and manage deployments, auto-scaling (HPA), and load-balancing on Kubernetes (k8s) using Helm.
Build, maintain, and optimize secure GitHub Actions CI/CD deployment pipelines.
Observability & Reliability Engineering

About the role
We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus of the role is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements as needed, alongside supporting existing entities and reinsurance programmes where required. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build-focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady-state reporting.
Key responsibilities
Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) — defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, and ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet the requirements of the relevant regulator; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g. DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
Build the financial model for each new entity — three-statement model and entity-level profit and loss — establishing the management reporting suite from which ongoing reporting will run.
Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring the accounting treatment and control framework are correctly set up from inception; support existing programmes as required.
Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity-level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing the format, commentary structure and distribution; support the ongoing production of these for existing entities as required.
Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) — providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for completion of the annual capital setting process (ECM/SBF cycle), optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining the FAL headroom analysis relative to the approved capital requirement.
Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities — including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity — to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes — including letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits — ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed in line with programme terms and regulatory requirements.
Own the capital waterfall and inter-entity funding mechanics — managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, and ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
Produce the board-level capital reporting pack — including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes — on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, including covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day-to-day work.

description:

We are looking for a curious, research-oriented individual with a background in Psychology, Behavioural Science or Cognitive Science who can turn research findings into practical solutions.The role focuses on understanding how engineers think, feel and behave toward AI, identifying the barriers to AI adoption, and helping turn AI usage into a consistent daily habit.
A background in any one of these fields is sufficient; a combination of all three is not required. Mindset matters most.

Identify the fears, doubts, beliefs and motivations that influence how different engineer personas respond to AI.
Help document behavioural patterns and translate assessment findings into actionable insights.

Study how engineers learn, interact with and use AI tools in their daily work.
Explore when engineers trust, question, resist or ignore AI-generated outputs.
Identify patterns in learning, decision-making and problem-solving that influence AI adoption.
3. Behaviour Change & Intervention – Behavioural Science
Help design and implement persona-specific interventions to improve AI adoption.
Support experiments and practical initiatives that encourage consistent AI usage.
Track behavioural changes over time using observations, feedback and usage data.
Compare outcomes before and after interventions and recommend improvements based on the findings.
4. Research-to-Action & Reporting
Convert observations into clear hypotheses that can be tested using data.
Support the implementation of research findings
Document results, identify what works and what does not, and communicate clear, decision-ready conclusions.
Refine approaches when evidence shows that an intervention is not effective.
Educational Qualifications
A bachelor's or master's degree in any one of the following fields (Final-semester students from the above disciplines are welcome to apply.)
Psychology (Organisational, Applied, Cognitive, Counselling or any other specialisation)
Behavioural Science or Behavioural Economics
Cognitive Science
Added Advantage
Certification or coursework in behavioural science, behavioural economics, psychometrics or change management.
Research experience through a dissertation, thesis, academic project or publication.
Familiarity with surveys, behavioural assessments, qualitative research or basic data analysis.

Product Manager
2Base Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a Kochi-based IT services and software development company established in 2010. We are a full-service technology partner offering technology consulting, custom software development, enterprise application development, web and mobile application development, and digital transformation solutions. We have delivered across Insurance, EdTech, Hospitality, and Travel & Tourism, and we work with clients in global markets including the US and UK.
The Opportunity
We are building our own technology products, with a strong focus on AI-driven solutions, and we are looking for the person who will own what they become. This is a product at the concept and early development stage. You will shape its direction, validate the market opportunity, decide what is built and what is not, and drive it towards commercial success.
As our first dedicated Product Management professional, you will also establish the product function at 2Base: there is no existing roadmap, process or product organisation to inherit.
Key Responsibilities
Define the product vision, strategy, roadmap and long-term direction, and keep the roadmap stable enough to plan against and open enough to change when the evidence changes.
Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer discovery to identify and validate product opportunities, and bring the findings into roadmap decisions rather than filing them as reports.
Translate customer problems and business needs into clear product requirements: the outcome and the user problem, specified well enough for Engineering to build against without dictating the solution.
Own feature prioritisation and release decisions with Engineering and UI/UX, and be able to state the cost and the benefit of each choice. A roadmap that only says yes is a backlog.
Identify and evaluate AI, Generative AI and automation opportunities, and assess each on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value before it reaches the roadmap.
Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.
Contribute to product positioning, pricing, go-to-market strategy and commercial viability, working with Sales and Marketing.
Build shared context across the organisation so that teams can make decisions without routing every question through you.
Work closely with the Founder, Engineering, UI/UX, Sales and other stakeholders to align on product direction and drive execution.
What You Will Not Own
​
Product Manager and Project Manager are used interchangeably across the market. At 2Base, they are different roles, so the boundary is stated rather than assumed.
Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.
Requirements
Experience
6–12 years in the technology industry, with at least 4 years in Product Management or direct product ownership.
At least one product you took from concept or early development to actual customer usage, with a clear view of what happened after release. A product you inherited fully formed and maintained is a weaker signal than a smaller one you shaped.
A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.
Direct work with engineering teams through a build, not across a handover, with enough understanding of software development, technical feasibility, APIs, integrations and cloud applications to judge what a decision will cost.
AI and Emerging Technology
Practical exposure to AI-powered products, Generative AI, machine learning or automation-driven solutions.
The ability to tell a capability apart from a product, and to assess an AI use case on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value rather than on novelty.
Product Judgement
You can describe how you decided what to build: the evidence you had, the evidence you wanted and did not have, and what you did about the gap.
You can reason about a product commercially. Who pays, what for, and what has to be true for the numbers to work.
You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.
You can make a decision that leaves someone unhappy, explain the reasoning, and keep working with them. Trade-offs are the job, and somebody loses every time one is made.
Education
A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
What We Are Not Looking For
Stated now rather than at the end of a multi-stage process.
Project or delivery managers looking to change title. The skills overlap less than the market suggests, and this is not a promotion path from delivery.
Business analysts who have written specifications against requirements someone else set. Valuable work; different work.
Candidates whose account of a product is the features it shipped, with no view on whether it should have shipped them.
Anyone who needs an established research function, design system and process in place before they can start.
Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

Product Manager
2Base Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a Kochi-based IT services and software development company established in 2010. We are a full-service technology partner offering technology consulting, custom software development, enterprise application development, web and mobile application development, and digital transformation solutions. We have delivered across Insurance, EdTech, Hospitality, and Travel & Tourism, and we work with clients in global markets including the US and UK.
The Opportunity
We are building our own technology products, with a strong focus on AI-driven solutions, and we are looking for the person who will own what they become. This is a product at the concept and early development stage. You will shape its direction, validate the market opportunity, decide what is built and what is not, and drive it towards commercial success.
As our first dedicated Product Management professional, you will also establish the product function at 2Base: there is no existing roadmap, process or product organisation to inherit.
Key Responsibilities
Define the product vision, strategy, roadmap and long-term direction, and keep the roadmap stable enough to plan against and open enough to change when the evidence changes.
Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer discovery to identify and validate product opportunities, and bring the findings into roadmap decisions rather than filing them as reports.
Translate customer problems and business needs into clear product requirements: the outcome and the user problem, specified well enough for Engineering to build against without dictating the solution.
Own feature prioritisation and release decisions with Engineering and UI/UX, and be able to state the cost and the benefit of each choice. A roadmap that only says yes is a backlog.
Identify and evaluate AI, Generative AI and automation opportunities, and assess each on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value before it reaches the roadmap.
Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.
Contribute to product positioning, pricing, go-to-market strategy and commercial viability, working with Sales and Marketing.
Build shared context across the organisation so that teams can make decisions without routing every question through you.
Work closely with the Founder, Engineering, UI/UX, Sales and other stakeholders to align on product direction and drive execution.
What You Will Not Own
​
Product Manager and Project Manager are used interchangeably across the market. At 2Base, they are different roles, so the boundary is stated rather than assumed.
Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.
Requirements
Experience
6–12 years in the technology industry, with at least 4 years in Product Management or direct product ownership.
At least one product you took from concept or early development to actual customer usage, with a clear view of what happened after release. A product you inherited fully formed and maintained is a weaker signal than a smaller one you shaped.
A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.
Direct work with engineering teams through a build, not across a handover, with enough understanding of software development, technical feasibility, APIs, integrations and cloud applications to judge what a decision will cost.
AI and Emerging Technology
Practical exposure to AI-powered products, Generative AI, machine learning or automation-driven solutions.
The ability to tell a capability apart from a product, and to assess an AI use case on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value rather than on novelty.
Product Judgement
You can describe how you decided what to build: the evidence you had, the evidence you wanted and did not have, and what you did about the gap.
You can reason about a product commercially. Who pays, what for, and what has to be true for the numbers to work.
You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.
You can make a decision that leaves someone unhappy, explain the reasoning, and keep working with them. Trade-offs are the job, and somebody loses every time one is made.
Education
A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
What We Are Not Looking For
Stated now rather than at the end of a multi-stage process.
Project or delivery managers looking to change title. The skills overlap less than the market suggests, and this is not a promotion path from delivery.
Business analysts who have written specifications against requirements someone else set. Valuable work; different work.
Candidates whose account of a product is the features it shipped, with no view on whether it should have shipped them.
Anyone who needs an established research function, design system and process in place before they can start.
Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

CookieYes is a consent management platform used by over a million websites to stay compliant with GDPR, CCPA and a growing list of global privacy regulations. RESPONSIBILITIES
Own the growth plan and its implementation. Set quarterly targets across acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention, sequence the work, and be accountable for shipping it rather than presenting it.

We are building our own technology products, with a strong focus on AI-driven solutions, and we are looking for the person who will own what they become. This is a product at the concept and early development stage. Key Responsibilities

Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer discovery to identify and validate product opportunities, and bring the findings into roadmap decisions rather than filing them as reports.
Translate customer problems and business needs into clear product requirements: the outcome and the user problem, specified well enough for Engineering to build against without dictating the solution.

Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.

Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.

A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.

AI and Emerging Technology

You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.

About the role
We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus of the role is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements as needed, alongside supporting existing entities and reinsurance programmes where required. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build-focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady-state reporting.
Key responsibilities
Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) — defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, and ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet the requirements of the relevant regulator; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g. DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
Build the financial model for each new entity — three-statement model and entity-level profit and loss — establishing the management reporting suite from which ongoing reporting will run.
Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring the accounting treatment and control framework are correctly set up from inception; support existing programmes as required.
Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity-level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing the format, commentary structure and distribution; support the ongoing production of these for existing entities as required.
Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) — providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for completion of the annual capital setting process (ECM/SBF cycle), optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining the FAL headroom analysis relative to the approved capital requirement.
Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities — including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity — to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes — including letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits — ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed in line with programme terms and regulatory requirements.
Own the capital waterfall and inter-entity funding mechanics — managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, and ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
Produce the board-level capital reporting pack — including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes — on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, including covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day-to-day work.
